title: Sections over a w-contractible affine are exact
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $D$ w-contractible be an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$,
and let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. The functor
$\Gamma(U,-)\colon F\mapsto F(U)$ from abelian sheaves (or from sheaves of
$\mathcal R$-modules) to abelian groups (or $\mathcal R(U)$-modules) is exact.

proof.text: Transport abelian sheafification and its locally-bijective equivalence criterion from a small model of the pro-etale site in the section universe max v (t+1). The site itself has object universe t+1 and hom universe t, so essentiallySmallSelf supplies this smallness. Evaluation on abelian sheaves preserves finite limits because sheafToPresheaf and presheaf evaluation do. Evaluation on module sheaves preserves finite limits by the existing sectionwise-limits instance. Both evaluation functors are additive by sectionwise addition.

For an epimorphism g of abelian sheaves, the general-site abelian epi/local-surjectivity criterion gives local surjectivity. Forgetting addition gives a locally surjective morphism of set sheaves. Apply the already proved source isWeaklyContractible_of_iso at the identity isomorphism Spec D = Spec D, in the same arbitrary section universe. Its surjectivity conclusion makes the evaluated group homomorphism epic. This uses the projectivity argument directly and avoids passing through set-sheaf epimorphisms.

The declared moduleSheaves_colimits_forgetful theorem supplies preservation of finite colimits by SheafOfModules.toSheaf R. Hence an epimorphism of module sheaves is an epimorphism on underlying abelian sheaves. Step 2 gives surjectivity on sections; the same underlying map is the evaluated module homomorphism, so the latter is epic as well.

For each evaluation functor apply Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels to the finite-limit preservation of step 1 and epimorphism preservation of steps 2 and 3. Additivity and preservation of homology imply preservation of finite colimits by Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology. Combine these two colimit assertions with the two finite-limit assertions to obtain the unchanged four-part conclusion.
